presentingComplaint: Sudden onset right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking, witnessed 55 minutes prior to arrival.
history: 68-year-old man with known hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and atrial fibrillation (not on anticoagulation, self-discontinued warfarin 6 months ago) was found by his wife suddenly unable to move his right arm and leg and slurring his speech while having breakfast. Last known well time is well documented at 55 minutes before ED arrival. No recent trauma, surgery, or GI bleeding. No seizure activity witnessed. No headache reported. Wife activated EMS immediately; stroke code called en route.
examination: Alert but anxious, expressive aphasia with preserved comprehension. Right facial droop (lower face). Right arm drift to 0/5 power, right leg 1/5 power. Left gaze preference. NIHSS scored at 14 (facial palsy 2, arm 4, leg 3, aphasia 2, dysarthria 1, sensory 1, neglect 1). No neck stiffness. Cardiac exam: irregularly irregular rhythm, no murmurs. No signs of active bleeding. Pupils equal and reactive.
imaging: Non-contrast CT head: no acute hemorrhage, ASPECTS 9, early loss of grey-white differentiation in left insular ribbon
CT angiogram head/neck: left M1 middle cerebral artery occlusion
CT perfusion: small core infarct with large penumbra (mismatch ratio >1.8), favorable for reperfusion therapy
finalDiagnosis: Acute ischaemic stroke, left MCA (M1) territory, cardioembolic (atrial fibrillation), within IV thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy window
citations: AHA/ASA Guideline for Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke 2019 (with 2023 update)
contraindications: Confirm no anticoagulant use within therapeutic window / INR <1.7 before thrombolysis
Exclude hemorrhage on non-contrast CT before tPA/tenecteplase
Screen for recent major surgery, GI bleed, or trauma within 14-21 days
BP must be controlled <185/110 mmHg prior to thrombolysis
Platelet count and glucose must be checked (glucose <50 or >400 mg/dL alters diagnostic certainty)
edgeCases: Wake-up strokes or unclear onset time require perfusion/DWI-FLAIR mismatch imaging to determine eligibility
Large vessel occlusion (M1) within 24h may qualify for mechanical thrombectomy even outside the standard IV thrombolysis window if favorable perfusion mismatch present
Atrial fibrillation without anticoagulation is a major cardioembolic risk factor and should prompt cardiac monitoring and anticoagulation planning after the acute phase
This case is a vascular/neurological emergency rather than an infective syndrome, so the stewardship/antimicrobial tier is not applicable (null)
expectedMaiK: MaiK should flag this as a time-critical stroke code: confirm last-known-well time, rule out hemorrhage and mimics, and prioritize IV thrombolysis/thrombectomy eligibility screening; antimicrobial stewardship is not applicable.
expectedNextQuestions: Exact last known well time and any anticoagulant/antiplatelet use
Blood glucose and INR/aPTT before thrombolysis decision
Eligibility for IV thrombolysis (tPA/tenecteplase) vs mechanical thrombectomy given M1 occlusion
Baseline functional status and pre-existing disability
Plan for cardiac monitoring and anticoagulation given atrial fibrillation
expectedInvestigations: CT perfusion or MRI DWI/FLAIR if onset unclear
Echocardiogram (after acute phase) for cardioembolic source
